resources.string: Trackhop
Trackhop ships without service keys. Create your own free key on the service\'s developer page: it takes about two minutes and the app guides you step by step.

When a track carries no ISRC (web routes, files), Trackhop looks it up once in Deezer\'s public catalogue, so Spotify, Apple Music and TIDAL answer with the exact recording instead of a look-alike. Anonymous request, no account involved.
Trackhop follows the system language: English, Italian, French, German, Spanish, Portuguese, Polish, Russian, Turkish, Chinese, Japanese, Korean.

Trackhop ships without keys of its own: Spotify, YouTube Music, TIDAL, Deezer, Last.fm and Apple Music connect through a free key created in your name, so their limits and quotas are yours alone. Here you can see and change them.
Trackhop is free with no subscriptions. It is supported by a single small banner ad; no data is sold and nothing leaves your phone except the requests to the music services you connect.
Saved inside Trackhop: use “Save as file” here, or Options → Files, to get a CSV or M3U.

%1$d of %2$d tracks searched, then the service asked for a longer pause (%3$s). This is a limit of the service, not a Trackhop error: what was found has been applied and remembered. Run the sync again in a few minutes to continue from there.
the phone could not reach the service (DNS failed). Check the connection, any VPN or private DNS, and that Trackhop is allowed to use data in the background, then try again.
Describe a playlist; your own AI writes it, Trackhop finds the tracks.

Describe the playlist you want and your own AI writes it; Trackhop then looks the tracks up on the service you choose, like a normal sync, so anything the AI got wrong ends up among the tracks to review. Trackhop has no AI of its own: you connect yours (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini or any OpenAI-compatible server, even a local one) with a key from your account, and only the text you type here is sent to it.

Free to try: Google Gemini and Groq have a free tier, OpenRouter has free models (the ones ending in “:free”). A key takes a minute on the provider\'s site. Trackhop cannot ship a shared key: it would be visible in the open source code and used up within a day.

Trackhop already keeps dated backups of your playlists inside the app. Pick a folder (SD card, Nextcloud, Drive, any app that offers one) and the new versions are copied there too, so they survive the phone. To restore, import a file from that folder in Files.
Some phones (Xiaomi, Huawei, Oppo, Samsung) stop background apps. Exclude Trackhop from battery optimisation so the schedule is respected.
Your credentials stay encrypted on this phone. Trackhop only talks to the server you enter here.
You will sign in on %1$s, in your browser. Trackhop never sees your password.
You will sign in on %1$s\'s own page, shown inside the app. Trackhop never sees your password, only the session it leaves.
You will sign in with your Apple ID in Apple\'s own window. Trackhop never sees your password.
Your server details stay encrypted on this phone. Trackhop only talks to your server.
Trackhop only receives a limited, revocable permission, stored encrypted on this phone (Android Keystore).
There is no Trackhop server: data travels only between this phone and %1$s.

You sign in on the service\'s own page, as you would in a browser: Trackhop never sees your password, it only keeps the session, encrypted on this phone. Nothing to create. Not an official interface: it can stop working when the site changes.

You sign in on the service\'s own page, as in a browser: Trackhop never sees your password, only the session, encrypted on this phone. No official API exists: it can stop working when the site changes.
Passwords are typed on the services\' own pages, never in Trackhop.
Trackhop keeps only revocable access tokens, encrypted with the Android Keystore.
There is no Trackhop server and no account to create: nothing leaves your phone except requests to the services you connect.
It leaves the phone only towards %1$s, with each request you make. Trackhop has no server of its own: Options → Security → Connections lists every host this app has ever contacted, so you can check.
“Forget the key” deletes it at once. Safer still: create a key just for Trackhop, with a spending limit, and revoke it whenever you like.
Fingerprint, face or phone PIN before Trackhop opens.
Trackhop is locked
Daily limit set by YouTube (Google), not by Trackhop. Resets at midnight Pacific time. A search costs 100 units, adding a track 50.
Daily limit set by YouTube (Google), not by Trackhop, shared by everyone using the built-in key: what other users consume is not counted here. Your own credentials give you a quota of your own.
Welcome to Trackhop
You sign in on each service\'s own page. Trackhop keeps only an encrypted, revocable token on this phone and has no server of its own.

Trackhop ships without service keys of its own: for Spotify, YouTube Music, TIDAL and Deezer you create a free key on the service\'s developer page, and the app walks you through it in about two minutes. Your data then flows only between your phone and your own key.
You log in on each service\'s official page. Trackhop never sees your password.
Sign in on %1$s\'s own page. Trackhop only receives the confirmation that comes back at the end.

Trackhop is free, with no subscriptions and no locked features. One small banner, never full-screen, pays for the developer\'s coffee and the hours spent keeping every service working. If it ever bothers you, open an issue on GitHub.
Trackhop is free, with no ads and no subscriptions. Nothing leaves the phone except the requests to the music services you connect.
Trackhop has no ads, no subscriptions and no locked features. It lives on voluntary contributions: if it saves you time, you can buy the developer a coffee.

Offer Trackhop for music links

A Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube Music, Amazon Music, Deezer or TIDAL link can then open in Trackhop, which adds the track to a playlist on any of your services. Android still asks which app to use, or keeps the one set in its link settings: Trackhop never takes a link by itself.
The colours of your wallpaper instead of Trackhop\'s own. The title banner keeps the brand colours.
%1$s does not say which tracks it can no longer play, so Trackhop cannot check here.
For each one Trackhop proposes a version that plays. Accept it, search another, remove the entry or skip it. Nothing changes until you apply.
%1$d tracks get a playable version, %2$d entries are removed. The originals stay in Trackhop\'s log so you can undo.
Once a week Trackhop looks through your playlists and tells you when a track can no longer be played. Nothing is changed by itself.
SoundCloud changed its web player; Trackhop needs an update
Shazam a lot? In Shazam\'s settings, connect Spotify or Apple Music: every song you Shazam lands in a “My Shazam Tracks” playlist. Trackhop can keep it in sync on any of your services.
